title: Copilot Studio: labelled and encrypted file uploads for agents on the Microsoft 365 channel
summary: Hold for two governance corrections: the label-encryption path omits navigation and a required scope choice, and the monitoring row describes automation as undocumented despite a documented activity export cmdlet. The roadmap facts and the existing Copilot Studio billing explanation are supported; upload-specific defaults and additional licensing remain unpublished.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to allow users to upload MPIP sensitivity-labelled files to Copilot Studio agents on the Microsoft 365 channel.
claims.quote: Unblock users from upload files with Microsoft Purview Information Protection (MPIP) sensitivity labels to Copilot Studio agents deployed on the M365 channel.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the planned labelled-upload feature itself.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio sensitivity labelled encrypted file uploads Microsoft 365 channel 571305 default enable permissions licensing'; opened image-input-analysis, ai-copilot-studio and billing-licensing; results describe current encrypted-file restrictions, not the planned support.

claims.where: summary; What's changing: Today's documented behaviour
claims.claim: The current file-input documentation says encrypted files, including sensitivity-label encryption, are unsupported.
claims.quote: Files with encryption, such as sensitivity labels or password protection, aren't supported.

claims.claim: Uploading an encrypted or password-protected Office file produces a message that it cannot be read.
claims.quote: When a user uploads a password-protected or encrypted Office file, the agent tells the user that the file is encrypted or password-protected and can't be read.

claims.claim: Some rights-managed or label-encrypted files produce a generic error instead.
claims.quote: For some rights-managed or label-encrypted files, the agent returns a generic error instead.

claims.claim: The file-input article describes agents powered by the standard harness.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.claim: The standard harness is a Copilot Studio agent runtime.
claims.quote: The standard harness and the Microsoft Copilot harness are two authoring and runtime options in Copilot Studio.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/guidance/choose-harness to sources, or remove the parenthesis '(a Copilot Studio agent runtime)'.

claims.where: What's changing: Microsoft Copilot Chat alternative
claims.claim: The file-input documentation points users to Microsoft Copilot Chat for sensitivity-labelled files.
claims.quote: or use a Microsoft 365 experience such as Microsoft Copilot Chat, which supports sensitivity-labeled files.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels make an agent available in Teams and Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote: you can connect it to the Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Teams channels so users can chat with it in both Teams and Microsoft Copilot.

claims.where: What's changing: Related Purview behaviour; Risk assessment
claims.claim: For the documented AI sensitivity-label protections, users need EXTRACT as well as VIEW when the label applies encryption.
claims.quote: When the sensitivity label applies encryption, users must have the EXTRACT usage right, as well as VIEW, for the AI apps to return the data.

claims.claim: The Purview Copilot Studio article documents encryption support only for sensitivity labels and the SharePoint knowledge source.
claims.quote: Encryption is supported only with sensitivity labels, and only for the SharePoint knowledge source.

claims.claim: The SharePoint troubleshooting article instead says the agent cannot extract or ground on encrypted content.
claims.quote: However, the agent can't extract or ground on content whose protection encrypts the file.

claims.claim: The person applying encryption always retains EXTRACT as Rights Management owner.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Maker-built flows, connectors and tools can pass uploaded files to downstream services including SharePoint and ServiceNow.
claims.quote: Optionally, you can add logic in your flow to send this file to SharePoint, ServiceNow, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and similar services.

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document a sensitivity-label check at the uploaded-file hand-off to tools and flows.

claims.claim: Copilot and agents have documented access restrictions for unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive when they're labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions

claims.claim: A default sensitivity label extending SharePoint permissions is an exception to that restriction, with EXTRACT still required.
claims.quote: unless the label is used as a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.claim: Directly referencing a file by typing '/' is the other documented exception, also requiring EXTRACT.
claims.quote: or they're directly referenced by typing "/" (and in both cases, the user has EXTRACT permissions).

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[2].note; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Label-based Copilot DLP coverage for Copilot Studio agents is documented for SharePoint knowledge sources.
claims.quote: When the knowledge source is SharePoint, a DLP policy scoped to the Microsoft 365 Copilot location can restrict agents built in Copilot Studio for Microsoft Teams, SharePoint, and Microsoft 365 Copilot from processing sensitive content based on a specified sensitivity label.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: DLP does not scan file contents uploaded directly into Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur. DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.claim: The licensing model is mixed: ordinary Copilot Credits consumption and qualifying Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed usage inclusion.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the common currency across Copilot Studio capabilities. You can get them through pay-as-you-go meters, prepurchase plans, and Copilot Credit prepaid pack subscriptions.

claims.claim: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort needed to retrieve information, respond and use actions.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits measure the time and effort your agent needs to retrieve information, respond to prompts, and use any actions or custom Azure Bot Service skills.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: generative answer rate
claims.claim: The published generative-answer feature rate is 2 Copilot Credits, subject to the documented licensed-usage inclusion.
claims.quote: | Generative answer^2^ | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Classic answers, generative answers and Microsoft Graph tenant grounding in Copilot Chat, Teams or SharePoint are not charged for Microsoft 365 Copilot-licensed users when the agent uses their authenticated identity.
claims.quote: If you have a Microsoft 365 Copilot license, using agents in Copilot Chat, Microsoft Teams, or SharePoint for classic answers, generative answers, or Microsoft Graph tenant grounding isn't charged when the agent runs with your authenticated identity.

claims.where: Scope: Existing file-input setting; controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: File uploads is an existing maker-selected, per-agent setting.
claims.quote: Makers can allow users of their agent to upload files during chat interactions with their agent.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not explained how the planned labelled-file support interacts with the existing File uploads setting.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio sensitivity labelled encrypted file uploads Microsoft 365 channel 571305 default enable permissions licensing'; read image-input-analysis and the roadmap; no interaction between the planned labelled support and the current maker setting was specified.

claims.claim: No separate tenant or agent switch for the planned labelled-file uploads is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio sensitivity labelled encrypted file uploads Microsoft 365 channel 571305 default enable permissions licensing' and 'Copilot Studio File uploads setting API Dataverse bot configuration file upload enable'; read image-input-analysis and the Agent (bot) reference; no switch found.

claims.claim: Existing file input is configured in Copilot Studio at Settings > Generative AI > File processing capabilities > File uploads.
claims.quote: Go to the Settings page for your agent, and select Generative AI. ... Navigate to the File processing capabilities section. ... Turn on File uploads.

claims.claim: An API equivalent for the existing File uploads setting is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Copilot Studio File uploads setting API Dataverse bot configuration file upload enable' and 'Dataverse bot entity reference configuration file uploads FileUploadEnabled'; read image-input-analysis and searched the Agent (bot) reference for upload/file/configuration; no deciding property found.

claims.claim: The stated Purview DLP path reaches the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location through the Custom policy template.
claims.quote: Go to Data Loss Prevention > Policies and select + Create policy. ... Select the Custom template, then Custom policy. ... On the Locations page, set the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork location to on.
claims.fix: The path reaches the correct policy page but stops before its label-based control. Append '> rule > Content contains > Sensitivity labels > Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content', using the condition and action documented on the same page.

claims.claim: The printed New-DLPCompliancePolicy and New-DLPComplianceRule calls create a Copilot policy and an ExcludeContentProcessing blocking rule when the documented variables are defined.
claims.quote: New-DLPCompliancePolicy -Name "Copilot Policy" -Locations $loc -EnforcementPlanes @("CopilotExperiences") ... New-DLPComplianceRule -Name "Copilot Rule" -Policy "Copilot Policy" -AdvancedRule $advrule -RestrictAccess @(@{setting="ExcludeContentProcessing";value="Block"})

claims.claim: The label-based rule condition is Content contains > Sensitivity labels.
claims.quote: create DLP policies that use the Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork policy location with the Content contains > Sensitivity labels condition to exclude items from being processed.

claims.claim: The printed label-encryption route gives the complete choices needed to reach Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: Follow the general instructions to create or edit a sensitivity label and make sure the Files & other data assets option is selected for the label's scope
claims.fix: Replace the path with 'Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > label > Edit label > Define the scope for this label > Files & other data assets > Choose protection settings for the types of items you selected > Control access > Access control > Configure access control settings > Assign permissions now'. Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-sensitivity-labels to sources for the portal navigation and edit steps; retain encryption-sensitivity-labels as docs. The current route omits portal navigation and the scope choice that enables these settings.

claims.claim: Set-Label with EncryptionEnabled true, EncryptionProtectionType Template and EncryptionRightsDefinitions configures admin-defined encryption rights.
claims.quote: The EncryptionRightsDefinitions parameter specifies the rights users have ... This parameter is meaningful only when the EncryptionEnabled parameter value is either $true or $false and the EncryptionProtectionType parameter value is Template.

claims.claim: The Purview UI displays EXTRACT as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, the EXTRACT usage right is displayed as Copy and extract content(EXTRACT).

claims.claim: The portal route for enabling sensitivity labels for SharePoint and OneDrive is Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels > Turn on now.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Sensitivity labels. ... If you see a message to turn on the ability to process content in Office online files, select Turn on now

claims.claim: Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true enables the documented SharePoint and OneDrive sensitivity-label integration.
claims.quote: To enable the new capabilities, use the Set-SPOTenant cmdlet with the EnableAIPIntegration parameter: ... Set-SPOTenant -EnableAIPIntegration $true

Wait at least a day for policy data.' Keep api null only for that particular summary report, not for monitoring interactions generally. The cited ai-copilot-studio article explicitly connects these report graphs to their underlying activity-explorer events.

claims.claim: Microsoft instructs administrators to wait at least a day for policy data before viewing report results.
claims.quote: Wait at least a day for data, and then navigate to the Reports page to view the results of your policy.

claims.claim: Purview Data Security AI Admin is among the roles that can create or edit DLP policies for the Copilot location.
claims.quote: Accounts with one of the following roles or role groups can create or edit a DLP policy ... Purview Data Security AI Admin - Role for editing Data Loss Prevention policies related to Copilot
